newsitem.title: UK: Inspec says H1 profits grew despite stg hit.
newsitem.headline: Inspec says H1 profits grew despite stg hit.

text.p: British specialist chemicals company Inspec Group Plc said on Tuesday the "unremitting" strength of sterling cut pre-tax profits in the first six months of 1997 by around 5.0 million stg.
But this was more than compensated for by focusing on "fixed costs, volume growth, prudent raw material purchasing and improved productivity," the company said in a statement.
"Despite the adverse effect of currency, Inspec's performance was highly creditable with solid organic growth being achieved across the group," chairman John Hollowood said in the results statement.
"We are continuing to focus our energies on driving organic growth and reducing debt. I am confident that the good progress we have made will continue in the second half."
The group reported a 57 percent jump in pre-tax profits to 24.7 million stg in the six months to June 30. It proposed a 7.1 percent increase in the interim dividend to 2.25 pence a share.
The group's net debt was reduced to 130 million stg from 149.8 million at the end of 1996.
